_comment: Source of truth for the build loop. CLAUDE.md reads this at the start of every session. Don't hand-edit gate results — they're written by scripts/check_*_gate.py so they reflect what was actually measured, not what someone hoped for.

inference_pool.threshold: Groq (primary tier, spec §6) succeeds on judging AND architecture task-shaped prompts. Workers AI status is recorded but not required to pass.

build_pipeline.threshold: The .github/workflows/team-build-turn.yml workflow completes successfully at least once, per spec §8

details.inference_router: src/router.ts, verified live via POST /inference (Groq primary)

details.rag_memory: Vectorize-backed, agent-scoped recall verified (0.79-0.83 similarity on relevant queries, confirmed no cross-agent leakage)
details.research: Tavily only (free forever, no card) — Exa tried and dropped after cost/alternative research, see project memory 2026-07-21

details.queue: event_queue table, atomic UPDATE...RETURNING claiming (D1 has no FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED but doesn't need one — single-primary serialized writes), ported from ideaconnect
details.scheduler_executor_split: scheduler.ts never calls an LLM, only decides what's due; executor.ts claims + dispatches + calls the router, ported from ideaconnect
phases_verified_live: deep_research (12 agents queued, real ones completed via the LIVE cron trigger autonomously, unprompted)
architecture (real build plans generated matching spec's tech-stack/components/risks/fallback format)
details.self_healing: resetStuckItems verified — force-orphaned an in_progress row, confirmed it was reset to pending and successfully reprocessed within the same tick
details.real_bug_found_and_fixed: router.ts TASK_MODELS had no Workers AI fallback for 'design'/'validate' task types, causing hard failures during a Groq burst instead of falling through per spec §6 — added the missing fallbacks
details.not_in_scope: hackathon team formation / build-turn GitHub Actions dispatch is week4_build_system per the roadmap

details.github_org: AI-arena-hackathon (spec §12: one org, one repo per hackathon team)
details.team_formation: src/events/executor.ts handleTeamFormation — picks top 2 architecture_complete ideas by critique count from the parent ideathon, creates+scaffolds each team's repo, dispatches first build turn same day (spec §3.2 Day 1)
details.hackathon_phase_logic: src/events/scheduler.ts hackathonPhaseForDay — team_formation (day 0) -> building (day 1-2, one dispatch/team/day) -> ready_for_judging (day 3+)
details.observatory_build_status: GET /admin/events/:id/build-status (spec §11), polls GitHub Actions job status per team
bugs_found_and_fixed_via_live_testing: @noble/hashes/blake2b import path stale for installed v2.2.0 (-> @noble/hashes/blake2.js)
auto_init:true on team repo creation collided with our own scaffold PUTs (GitHub requires sha to update a file auto_init already created) -- removed auto_init
parallel scaffold-file writes raced to create the repo's first commit/branch, causing intermittent 409s -- made sequential
dispatch.ts hardcoded ref:master but non-auto_init repos default to main
details.verified_live: created hackathon event_391eac5c-2523-4743-b9f5-76afeca3a8a7 from real ideathon event_2eaf0bb2-0f84-48b6-b781-7b5836e0a67a; both team repos created under AI-arena-hackathon, scaffolded, secrets set; both teams' first build-turn GitHub Actions runs completed with conclusion=success
details.retry_safety_hardened_2026_07_22: team_formation is now idempotent per-team (hackathon_teams.status forming->building gate, createTeamRepo tolerates 422 already-exists by reusing the repo, putFile skips files that already exist) -- verified live by re-queuing team_formation for the already-complete test event and confirming zero duplicate repos/dispatches (identical GitHub Actions run IDs before and after)
details.also_did: upgraded wrangler 3.90 -> 4.112 + @cloudflare/workers-types v5 peer dep, both required for continued Cloudflare API compatibility

details.2026_07_24_verification: Workers AI daily quota reset (new UTC day) let the self-healing retry finish without any code changes. Confirmed live: GET /events/event_cd9644ef-a78a-4758-8f65-53c76995bb5c now status=complete with a real winner_team_id. GET /events/event_cd9644ef-a78a-4758-8f65-53c76995bb5c/tribunal shows all 3 stages present for all 12 agents: 12 individual reflections, 12 cross-examinations, 12 syntheses, real content, timestamps 2026-07-23T19:21-19:36 UTC. This closes the 'not yet observed to finish' item from 2026-07-23 -- ideathon judging, hackathon judging, and the full 3-stage Tribunal are all now verified live end to end. Cold Storage Rollover (spec section 15.1) remains explicitly deferred (not a gate blocker, same precedent as Week 4) -- D1 is nowhere near the 80%-of-5GB trigger to meaningfully test it yet.
details.2026_07_23_update: Full 3-agent code review applied (docs/CODE_REVIEW_2026-07-22.md): fixed real network exposure in team-build-turn.yml (Squid proxy + DOCKER-USER iptables, verified live), retry-safety backported to remaining scheduler phases, judge_scores dedup, calibration visibility, /inference auth, plus a full code-quality pass and Groq reasoning_effort=low (verified live, fixes the reasoning-truncation root cause). Separately: hackathon judging (judge_team) completed fully live -- event_cd9644ef-a78a-4758-8f65-53c76995bb5c reached status=judged with a real winner_team_id determined by weighted score. Then found 2 MORE live bugs in Tribunal's own completion-detection (isStageComplete counted all-time failed rows, permanently blocking advancement even after every agent succeeded; ensureTribunalCrossExamAndSynthesis's retry loop stopped running entirely once all 12 agents had been queued once, a permanent stall for any single failure) -- both fixed, plus a 30-min retry backoff added (676 wasted retries were observed hammering an exhausted Workers AI quota every 5 min before the fix). Verified live: the stuck event advanced from judged to tribunal on the next tick post-fix. Individual reflections (12/12) and hackathon judging are fully verified complete; cross-examination and synthesis are queued and self-healing but not yet observed to finish (still gated on the same Workers AI quota, now with proper backoff -- no code changes needed to finish this, just quota headroom).
details.judges: src/judges/personas.ts, 7 judges with per-phase weights (ideathon/hackathon columns sum to 1.0 each), spec §13
details.calibration: src/judges/calibration.ts, 3 anchor ideas x 7 judges, Pearson correlation gate (>=0.6), spec §13/§16 — runs once per event before real judging
details.scoring: src/judges/scoring.ts scoreTarget, idempotent (checks existing judge_scores rows before re-scoring)
details.tribunal: src/tribunal/reflection.ts — individual reflection -> cross-examination (paired with whoever critiqued them most) -> synthesis, synthesis embeds into Vectorize (type=reflection) so lessons are recallable in future events per spec §14's "carry into the next event"
details.archive_query: POST /archive/query added (spec §10/§15) — semantic search over the same Vectorize index agent memory + tribunal reflections already write to, optional agentId/eventId/type filters
details.verified_live_ideathon_judging: event_2eaf0bb2-0f84-48b6-b781-7b5836e0a67a: calibration ran (correlation computed, passed), all 6 architecture_complete ideas judged with real 7-judge weighted scores (avg 6.5-7.0 range), event transitioned to status=judged. A NEW hackathon event created from it correctly picked the top 2 by real ideathon_score (7.05, 6.9) — replaces Week 4's critique-count proxy per the plan noted at that gate's pass.
details.not_yet_verified_live: hackathon judging (judge_team) and the full 3-stage Tribunal — both deployed and exercised partially (judge_team ran successfully for demonstrating real build-turn-outcome grounding, one team's failed build turn genuinely showed up in its scoring context) but full completion is blocked by today's Cloudflare Workers AI daily Neuron allocation being genuinely exhausted from this session's extensive live testing (confirmed: Groq's judging model still has ~800/1000 daily requests of headroom; Workers AI's real account-wide 10,000 Neuron/day cap is what's hit — not a code defect, the router's own DAILY_CAPS tracking undercounts because agents/memory.ts's embed() calls aren't recorded against it, a real but separate gap worth fixing later). Self-healing retry is in place (per-team idempotent check in scheduler.ts) — will complete automatically once quota resets (next UTC day) or Groq capacity absorbs the load, no code changes needed to finish this.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_via_live_testi: calibration's max_tokens:100 (and scoring's 300) were nowhere near enough for judging's reasoning-model tier (gpt-oss-120b / deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b) to finish hidden <think> reasoning before the visible JSON answer -- bumped both to 700, matching executor.ts callAgent's already-proven budget for this same model class
extractJson never stripped <think>...</think> reasoning blocks -- added (ideaconnect precedent the Arena had never actually ported despite router.ts's own comment citing it)

judging's Workers AI fallback model (deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b) is a verbose reasoning model unsuited to short structured-JSON tasks -- swapped to llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast, matching architecture's already-stable fallback choice

firing 21 (calibration) or 5-batch x 7 (scoring) concurrent LLM calls hit Workers' "stalled HTTP response canceled to prevent deadlock" protection -- reduced calibration to 7-way concurrency (parallel across judges, sequential per judge's 3 anchors)

D1 throws 'LIKE or GLOB pattern too complex' whenever a LIKE pattern contains a literal double-quote character -- every JSON-substring idempotency check in the codebase (judge_idea, judge_team, and a PRE-EXISTING Week 3/4 dispatch_build_turn check that had never actually been exercised against matching data yet) used exactly this pattern shape; replaced all 4 with fetch-then-filter-in-JS

router.ts trusted Groq/Workers AI API responses as always being a plain string via 'any' casts -- found live that content can come back non-string under conditions not fully pinned down, crashing downstream .slice()/.replace() calls; added typeof validation at the API boundary in router.ts itself rather than patching every consumer

processQueue's default batch limit (5) combined with judge_idea/judge_team's ~14 subrequests each (7 parallel LLM calls + 7 parallel DB inserts) exceeded Cloudflare's per-invocation subrequest limit -- reduced default to 3
details.deferred_not_implemented: Cold Storage Rollover (spec §15.1, monthly D1->R2 archival at 80% utilization) -- explicitly not attempted this pass; can't realistically trigger or verify the 80%-of-5GB condition at current data volumes (DB is ~0.35MB), same 'flag don't silently skip' call as Week 4's retry-safety gap

views_built_and_verified_live: Agent Graph (D3 force graph, real edges from archive_interactions)
Headroom Dashboard (real daily-cap gauges per provider/model)
Diff Viewer (real commits/diffs via GitHub API)
details.landing_page_redesigned_2026_07_24: Original had 7 stacked full-viewport scroll scenes with 5 different bespoke visual gimmicks -- replaced with one unified numbered rail component reused across all 5 event phases, per explicit user design feedback
details.nav_bug_fixed: Diff Viewer link was missing from every Observatory page's nav except diff.html itself
details.auto_deploy_wired_2026_07_24: Pages was never wired to auto-deploy on push -- every prior deploy was a manual `wrangler pages deploy`. Added .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml; user added CF_ACCOUNT_ID/CF_API_TOKEN repo secrets; manually dispatched to verify -- run 30192132698 completed with conclusion=success. Future pushes touching public/ now deploy automatically.

details.method: Compressed schedule via a new admin endpoint (PATCH /admin/events/:id/start-date) that backdates an event's start_date -- phase transitions are real calendar-day math (scheduler.ts) with no test-mode flag, deliberately: the beta needed to exercise the exact same production code path, just with a fast-forwarded clock. Actual work (LLM calls, real GitHub repos, real judging, real Tribunal) was 100% real throughout.
details.verified_live_full_cycle: ideathon event_e5415c58-99b1-4c96-aaca-6cd583c252e4: 12 agents' deep research -> 36 ideas -> critiques -> 6 architecture plans -> calibration -> 42/42 real judge scores -> status=judged. Hackathon event_f3601765-b9e9-4eb2-a568-9b17808e646c created from it: 2 real teams formed, 2 real repos under AI-arena-hackathon, both first build turns succeeded on GitHub Actions, both teams judged (14/14 scores), winner determined (team_00dae98f, alpha), full 3-stage Tribunal completed with ZERO failures (12 individual reflections, 12 cross-examinations, 12 syntheses), event reached status=complete.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_via_live_testi: handleSubmitIdea queued exactly 1 critic per idea despite the code's own comment citing spec section 4's 'critique 3 ideas not their own' -- confirmed live (33/36 ideas got exactly 1 critique, 3 got none, no retry-safety on the single enqueue call) -- fixed to queue 3 distinct critics

ensureIdeathonJudging/ensureHackathonJudging (judge_idea/judge_team) had NO retry backoff at all, unlike Tribunal's already-fixed shouldEnqueueForAgent -- confirmed live: with Workers AI genuinely over its daily cap, every 5-10s manual tick re-queued and re-failed all 6 ideas x 7 judges with zero recovery, the exact same retry-storm pathology already diagnosed for Tribunal just never ported here -- added backoff

DAILY_CAPS['workers_ai'] was an unmeasured guess (8500) below spec section 6's published 10,000/day -- confirmed live: app-tracked usage hit 8802 (over its own cap) while a direct real call against the Cloudflare account still succeeded fine -- raised to 9500

scoreTarget (judges/scoring.ts) used Promise.all across all missing judges -- one failed judge discarded every OTHER judge's successful result too, since the array rejected before the INSERT step ran. Confirmed live this repeatedly threw away 5-6 successful scores per retry under real inference pressure -- switched to Promise.allSettled, persisting whatever succeeds

Single Groq account meant 7 (judging) or 21 (calibration) concurrent LLM calls burst against one account's per-minute rate limit -- split Groq traffic across GROQ_API_KEY_1/2 (random) to halve the concurrent burst per account

Tribunal's 30-min retry backoff (Week 5 precedent) was ported to judging as-is, but that number was calibrated for genuine multi-hour daily-quota exhaustion (Tribunal's failure mode) -- judge_idea/judge_team failures are usually a single transient blip, not the whole event blocked for hours. Confirmed live: with the backoff shortened to 2 minutes, hackathon judging's one remaining failed judge (6/7 succeeded via the allSettled fix) cleared and completed within ~2 minutes instead of the 30 the old value would have required. The real cron's own 5-min cadence means anything under 5 min doesn't change production retry behavior anyway -- it only needed to outlast aggressive manual test-tick cadence, not the real failure's recovery time
details.admin_test_tooling_added: PATCH /admin/events/:id/start-date (bearer-token gated, same auth class as other /admin/events routes) -- reusable for any future compressed-schedule verification, not single-use scaffolding

details.why_this_gate_exists: docs/ARENA_BACKLOG.md's own suggestion -- add a new gate rather than reopen week7_closed_beta, so the roadmap's completed history stays intact. current_gate had read week7_closed_beta since 2026-07-27 while Part 1, Part 2, the Office rebuild and the autonomous cadence all landed, which misdirects every session that reads this file first.

landed.p0_0a: Root cause was NOT the sandbox (the earlier diagnosis was wrong). It is a non-string tool_call.id from Workers AI rejected by the Vercel AI SDK. Fixed by scripts/workers_ai_shim.js.
landed.stall_watchdog: MAX_ITEM_ATTEMPTS + checkForStalledEvents -- one permanently-failing item can no longer pin an event below terminal status and silently halt all future cadence.
landed.observatory: Agent Office rebuilt: failure/abandonment visible, hackathon team benches, artifact bubbles, Merge Tables, judges' bench, idle roaming, and eight per-phase environments. See docs/OFFICE_INVESTIGATION_2026-07-31.md.
landed.schema: 15 migrations tracked by scripts/apply_schema.js; production baselined and current.

real_bugs_found_and_fixed_via_live_produ: MAX_BUILD_TURNS_PER_DAY never once fired -- it counted with queuedPayloadValues, which returns a Set, so every team's dispatches-today was permanently 1 against a ceiling of 6. The live hackathon dispatched 226 turns on 2026-07-31 and 122 more by 06:25 on 08-01. Every health signal read green throughout: cron ticking, zero queue failures, no errors, watchdog seeing progress. Only the cancelled conclusions on the GitHub side gave it away.

createTeamRepo froze each team's build harness at repo-creation time, so every harness fix since reached nobody. The running teams' workflow predated run-name (which reconcileBuildTurns matches runs to turns by, hence mis-attributed conclusions) and predated the P0-0a shim entirely. Fixed by syncTeamHarness, driven off a HARNESS_FILES allowlist that can never touch a team's own code.

apply_schema.js read a batch summary as query results (wrangler d1 execute --file does not return rows), so every sentinel check answered 'present'. --baseline would have recorded all 15 migrations as applied, including 4 that were missing, then reported nothing to do.
details.not_yet_verified_live: Nothing in Part 2, the P0-0a shim, or the rebuilt Office has run against a live autonomous cycle -- every verification to date used seeded fixtures. The hackathon in flight (event_8088ef16) reaches ready_for_judging on 2026-08-01 and is the first real exercise of the judging path; the ideathon that auto-starts after it is the first fully autonomous cycle.

open_and_deliberately_deferred.G6: GET /events/:id/agent-activity returns one representative queue row per agent, so real parallelism is invisible in the Office.
open_and_deliberately_deferred.G7: The Office is a snapshot; Replay is a separate view. Journal-backed replay (AI Town's model) is the right fix and is a data-model change, not a view change.
open_and_deliberately_deferred.cold_storage_rollover: spec 15.1 -- D1 is ~2MB against an 80%-of-5GB trigger, still untestable.
open_and_deliberately_deferred.deploy_worker_workflow: RESOLVED 2026-08-01. deploy-worker.yml failed its first 8 runs because the workflow pinned setup-node to Node 20 and wrangler 4.x refuses to start below v22 ('Wrangler requires at least Node.js v22.0.0'). Nothing to do with credentials. Two successive guesses were wrong -- first that CF_API_TOKEN lacked Workers Scripts: Edit (it holds it, along with D1/Vectorize/R2/Pages/Workers AI), then that it needed Account Settings: Read or Workers Observability: Edit. deploy-pages.yml never hit this because it runs wrangler via npx on the runner's own newer Node with no setup-node pin. The failure was diagnosable only after the deploy step was changed to echo wrangler's error back as a GitHub ANNOTATION: job logs require an authenticated token, annotations do not, so on a public repo eight failures had reported nothing beyond 'Process completed with exit code 1'. Lesson worth keeping: when CI fails opaquely, make the failure self-reporting before theorising about causes.
open_and_deliberately_deferred.build_turns_correction: db/corrections/build_turns_event_8088ef16_2026-08-01.sql is reviewed and ready but NOT applied -- the production write is blocked by the sandbox classifier and needs a human to run it. Rationale in docs/BUILD_TURN_CORRECTION_2026-08-01.md.
